name: io.github.AnonymousOnyx22/student-citations-mcp
description: Citation generator MCP server. APA 7, MLA 9 and Chicago author date citations from a DOI, an ISBN or typed details, with in text citations. No account.

tools.name: format_citation
tools.description: Format a journal article, book, website, book chapter, thesis, report, dataset or preprint as a citation in APA 7, MLA 9, Chicago author date or IEEE, from details you provide. Inputs: type (journal, book, website, chapter, thesis, report, dataset or preprint), title, and optional authors (family plus given names), year, container, publisher, city, edition, editors, translators, volume, issue, pages, doi, url, date_text, accessed, institution, degree, repository, report_number and style (apa7, mla9, chicago-ad, ieee or all). Pass all to get all three styles in one reply, each one with its style name on the line above it. Editors and translators are for books and take the same shape as authors: a book with editors and no authors puts the editors where the author goes, and a book with authors too carries the other names after the title, in the spot each style uses. Example prompt: "Cite this journal article in APA 7: Learning to learn by John Kenneth Smith and Alice Jones, 2020, Journal of Study Skills, volume 4, issue 2, pages 11-25."

authors.description: List of authors with family and optional given names.

editors.description: Editors of a book or a chapter, same shape as authors. When a book has editors and no authors, they take the author's place in the citation.

translators.description: Translators of a book, same shape as authors.

container.description: Journal name, the book title for a chapter, or website name. Required for a journal article and for a chapter, since without it the citation would be missing the work it appears in.

city.description: Publisher city, used by Chicago for books.

date_text.description: Website date as you want it shown, like "2026, October 14" for APA or "14 Oct. 2026" for MLA.

institution.description: The university or organisation behind a thesis, a report or a dataset.

degree.description: The degree of a thesis, like "Ph.D.".

repository.description: Where a preprint was posted, like arXiv.

report_number.description: The number of a report or a standard.

style.description: Citation style. apa7, mla9, chicago-ad (Chicago author date), harvard or ieee, or all to get APA 7, MLA 9 and Chicago author date in one reply with a label above each one.

examples.output: Smith, J. K., & Jones, A. (2020). Learning to learn. *Journal of Study Skills*, *4*(2), 11-25.

tools.name: format_bibliography
tools.description: Format several sources at once as one works cited list, alphabetised by the first author's family name in APA 7, MLA 9 or Chicago author date, or numbered in citation order in IEEE. A source with no author is alphabetised by its title. Inputs: sources (an array of objects, each with the same fields as format_citation: type, title and optional authors, year, container, publisher, city, edition, editors, translators, volume, issue, pages, doi, url, date_text, accessed, institution, degree, repository and report_number), dois (a list of DOIs to look up on Crossref), isbns (a list of ISBNs to look up on Open Library), urls (a list of web addresses to fetch and cite as websites) and style (apa7, mla9, chicago-ad or ieee). Give sources, dois, isbns, urls or any mix, up to 50 lookups in one call. If one lookup fails the reply is an error that names it. Example prompt: "Put these three sources into an APA works cited list: a journal article by Smith and Jones from 2020, a book by Cormen from 2009 and a website from example.edu."

dois.description: DOIs to look up on Crossref and add to the list, each one a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539 or a doi.org link.

isbns.description: ISBNs to look up on Open Library and add to the list as books. Dashes are fine.

sources.description: The sources for the list. Each one takes the same fields as format_citation, so a journal article, a book, a website, a chapter, a thesis, a report, a dataset and a preprint can share one list.

authors.description: List of authors with family and optional given names.

editors.description: Editors of a book or a chapter, same shape as authors. When a book has editors and no authors, they take the author's place in the citation.

translators.description: Translators of a book, same shape as authors.

container.description: Journal name, the book title for a chapter, or website name. Required for a journal article and for a chapter, since without it the citation would be missing the work it appears in.

city.description: Publisher city, used by Chicago for books.

date_text.description: Website date as you want it shown, like "2026, October 14" for APA or "14 Oct. 2026" for MLA.

institution.description: The university or organisation behind a thesis, a report or a dataset.

degree.description: The degree of a thesis, like "Ph.D.".

repository.description: Where a preprint was posted, like arXiv.

report_number.description: The number of a report or a standard.

style.description: Citation style. apa7, mla9, chicago-ad (Chicago author date), harvard or ieee.

examples.output:
Cormen, T. H. (2009). *Introduction to algorithms* (3rd ed.). MIT Press.

Smith, J. K., & Jones, A. (2020). Learning to learn. *Journal of Study Skills*, *4*(2), 11-25.

tools.name: cite_from_doi
tools.description: Look up a DOI on Crossref and format the citation. The Crossref record decides the shape: a journal article, a book or an edited book, a book chapter or a conference paper, a thesis, a report, a dataset or a preprint. Inputs: doi (a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539 or a doi.org link) and style (apa7, mla9, chicago-ad, ieee or all). Pass all to get all three styles in one reply, each one with its style name on the line above it. Example prompt: "Cite 10.1038/nature14539 in APA."

doi.description: A DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, or a doi.org link.

style.description: Citation style. apa7, mla9, chicago-ad (Chicago author date), harvard or ieee, or all to get APA 7, MLA 9 and Chicago author date in one reply with a label above each one.

examples.output: (Example) Formatted MLA 9 citation from Crossref, followed by a blank line and (From Crossref. Check it against your style guide.)

tools.name: find_doi
tools.description: Search Crossref for the DOI of a paper or a book when you have its title but no DOI. Returns the best matches, 5 by default, each with its title, authors, year, container and DOI, so you can pick the right one and pass the DOI to cite_from_doi. Inputs: title (the title, or as much of it as you know), optional author (a family name to narrow the search) and optional limit (1 to 10 matches). Example prompt: "Find the DOI for the paper Deep learning by LeCun."

title.description: The title of the paper or book, or as much of it as you know.

author.description: An author's family name, to narrow the search.

limit.description: How many matches to return, 1 to 10.

examples.output:
1. Deep learning. LeCun, Bengio, Hinton. 2015. Nature. DOI: 10.1038/nature14539

(From Crossref. Check that the title and authors are the work you mean, then pass the DOI to cite_from_doi.)

tools.name: cite_from_isbn
tools.description: Look up an ISBN on Open Library and format the book citation in APA 7, MLA 9, Chicago author date or IEEE. Inputs: isbn (a 10 or 13 digit ISBN, dashes are fine) and style (apa7, mla9, chicago-ad or ieee). Example prompt: "Cite ISBN 978-0-262-03384-8 in MLA 9."

isbn.description: A 10 or 13 digit ISBN. Dashes are fine.

style.description: Citation style. apa7, mla9, chicago-ad (Chicago author date), harvard or ieee.

examples.output:
Cormen, Thomas H., and Charles E. Leiserson. *Introduction to Algorithms*. MIT Press, 2009.

(From Open Library. Check it against your style guide.)

tools.name: cite_from_url
tools.description: Fetch a web page and format it as a website citation in APA 7, MLA 9, Chicago author date or IEEE. It reads the page title, the site name and the date from the page. Inputs: url (a full web address), style (apa7, mla9, chicago-ad, ieee or all), and optional title, site_name and date to replace what the page gives. Pass all to get all three styles in one reply, each one with its style name on the line above it. Example prompt: "Cite this page in APA: https://example.edu/study."

url.description: A full web address, like https://example.edu/study.

style.description: Citation style. apa7, mla9, chicago-ad (Chicago author date), harvard or ieee, or all to get APA 7, MLA 9 and Chicago author date in one reply with a label above each one.

title.description: Use this title instead of the one on the page.

site_name.description: Use this site name instead of the one on the page.

date.description: Use this date instead of the one on the page, like 2026-10-14 or October 14, 2026.

examples.output:
*Study skills*. Example University. https://example.edu/study

(From the page. Check it against your style guide.)

tools.name: in_text_citation
tools.description: The in text citation that goes with a source, with an optional page number and an optional narrative form for a sentence where the author is named. Give authors and year, or a doi or an isbn and the record fills them in. Inputs: authors (family name plus optional given names), year, doi, isbn, page, form (parenthetical or narrative) and style (apa7, mla9, chicago-ad or ieee). A doi or an isbn cannot be combined with the other one. Example prompt: "Give the APA in text citation for Smith and Jones 2020 on page 14."

authors.description: List of authors with family and optional given names.

doi.description: A DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, or a doi.org link. The lookup fills in the authors and the year.

isbn.description: A 10 or 13 digit ISBN. Dashes are fine. The lookup fills in the authors and the year.

form.description: parenthetical is the usual brackets, like (Smith & Jones, 2020, p. 14). narrative puts the author in your sentence and keeps the rest in brackets, like Smith and Jones (2020, p. 14).

style.description: Citation style. apa7, mla9, chicago-ad (Chicago author date), harvard or ieee.
